dct_description_sm: These films were recovered to inform an ongoing historical-geographical study of minerals-driven Arctic industrial development and resettlement in Arctic regions. This portion of the project focused on the Rankin Inlet Nickel Mine (1958-62), significant as as one of the first deliberate attempts at the industrial employment of Aboriginal northerners, and the town was also connected to federal Inuit resettlement efforts. In addition to documentary and oral history research, visual records were sought of the mine during this period. These three films document in different ways the Inuit experience of mineral development at Rankin Inlet, and the subsequent experience of the community with mine closure and adjustment.
